acceptance: RED is the untouched primary failure: bash ops/tests/test_ios_ops_release_heartbeat.sh exits non-zero with ModuleNotFoundError for task_registry/ops. GREEN must make that command pass and keep the related streaming-command tests green.
acceptance_cmd: bash ops/tests/test_ios_ops_release_heartbeat.sh && uv run --no-project --python 3.13 --with pytest pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider ops/tests/test_streaming_command.py
brief: The iOS operations regression suite cannot start its shared command runner on a clean checkout, so the coverage gate reports a false baseline failure.
detail: 2026-08-11 Gate baseline investigation: ./ops/test_ops.sh ios-ops exits 1 even though test_ios_ops.sh completes 353 passed/0 failed. The first failing subcommand is ops/tests/test_ios_ops_release_heartbeat.sh. Its real stream capture starts ops/lib/streaming_command.py by absolute path; Python sets sys.path to ops/lib, so the runner cannot import its sibling ops/task_registry.py and its fallback import ops.task_registry also fails because the repository root is not on sys.path. Direct reproduction produces ModuleNotFoundError for task_registry and ops. This is a production runner import-path defect, not an Xcode availability or test-load failure. The same runner is used by the ios release workflow and gate heartbeat paths.
plan: Add a deterministic import seam in ops/lib/streaming_command.py based on the runner file location, so direct absolute-path execution can import sibling ops modules without relying on the caller cwd. Add a regression that invokes the real ios release heartbeat fixture from the repository root and asserts the structured heartbeat contract reaches rc=0; retain the existing task-registry import fallback only as a compatibility path. Do not add dependencies or copy production modules into fixtures.
scope: One Python runner import-path guard, one focused shell regression, and the existing streaming-command import tests.
